messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P1 -> Dedicated pool saturation detected for tenant=Everwell (everwell-prod-1). page: oncall-sre. Incident id=inc-4401234567
axel_sre: I'm on it. Checking pool stats now.
mike_infra: looking too — region us-east-1. everwell-prod-1 shows 8/8 GPUs active, gpu_util avg 98-100%. pending queue 381 requests. avg token latency 2.8s (baseline ~0.6s).
leila_se: Everwell reported user-facing timeouts and elevated 503s to their webhooks, they're seeing retries. Customer ops (everwell_ops) joined the channel.
everwell_ops: we started seeing errors ~10:12am PT, impacting our inference flows. We're on standby for mitigation steps.
axel_sre: quick assessment -> dedicated pool fully saturated. Autoscaler logs show no scale-out triggered in past 10m. Investigating autoscaler controller state.
olivia_reliability: if autoscaler is blocked, we should consider immediate burst from spare capacity to buy time. Do we have burst GPUs available in this region?
mike_infra: we have 2 burst-capable GPUs left in reserved pool (burst_budget=bb-117). Provision time ~3-5m for p4d instances to join cluster.
axel_sre: ok request immediate burst of +2 GPUs to everwell-prod-1. Also prepare a fallback route: for requests from tenant=everwell we can steer to a quantized model variant (llama-q4) if latency remains high. but prefer to add capacity first per customer preference.
leila_se: Everwell prefers capacity increases over model changes. Emma (account) is on the call with them.
emma_account: Everwell: they'd rather we avoid model changes; please prioritize burst. I'll tell them we're doing burst + monitoring.
axel_sre: running infra API to request burst now:
```
curl -X POST "https://infra.internal/api/v1/pools/everwell-prod-1/burst" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"extra_gpus":2, "reason":"inc-4401234567 - temporary burst"}'
```
system: deploy-bot: provisioning nodes for everwell-prod-1 (burst request bb-117) — request accepted. estimated join 4m.
mike_infra: provisioning logs: instance i-0a1b2c3 provisioned, gpu driver ok, container runtime started. join sequence started.
axel_sre: once nodes join I'll re-evaluate queue. setting alert silence for noisy 503s and forwarding to channel with updates.
system: metricsbot: pool everwell-prod-1 update -> gpu_util 99%, pending_queue 379 -> 120 (after first node join). avg rt trending down to 0.9s for served requests.
leila_se: customer notified: "we've added temporary capacity, monitoring; will provide ETA for full fix after root cause."
everwell_ops: thanks — seeing improvement already, about half of requests recovered. still some retries but much better.
olivia_reliability: autoscaler controller logs show scale-out was suppressed due to placement constraint tag: "isolate-tenant=true" plus a bug where the controller respected a max_nodes=8 cap specific to this pool. -> likely misconfig during recent config change.
axel_sre: noted. For immediate follow-up: 1) keep burst active until noon PT, 2) remove erroneous hard cap, 3) run a canary to ensure autoscaler triggers normally, 4) postmortem and RCA.
jonathan_sre: taking handoff for remediation and postmortem (covering next 6 hours). axel, I have the logs you flagged — will coordinate with infra to remove max_nodes cap, and add a safety rule to allow burst when queue>200 for >5m.
leila_se: file a support ticket for Everwell summary and timeline. include any customer-visible IDs and steps taken.
emma_account: filed support-#78421 and sent acknowledgement to the customer's security contact. they requested a follow-up call tomorrow for SLA impact.
axel_sre: final note — short-term metrics: after burst +1 node join pending_queue dropped 68%, error rate down to 1/s, 90th percentile latency ~1.1s. We avoided model fallback per customer's ask.
everwell_ops: appreciate the quick response. please include expected timeline for permanent fix in followup.
jonathan_sre: will own the permanent fix. adding remediation items to sprint and will update this thread with timeline. handoff complete — axel handing page to jonathan.
axel_sre: thanks all, leaving monitoring to jonathan. closing active pager for oncall-axel. followups in #postmortems once RCA is ready. :white_check_mark:
